project.name: Untitled Scenario
project.historicalContext:
he battlefield uses the existing frozen Rev C Pavia Engineering Master and compresses the historical battlefield to a 4 x 4 foot table while preserving the principal tactical relationships.

Important battlefield features include:

Mirabello Park walls and gates.
The Imperial breach in the northern portion of the park.
Castello Mirabello.
The Vernavola stream and associated wet ground.
The principal roads and avenues through the park.
Open parkland and cultivated ground.
Woods and hunting groves.
Orchards and gardens.
The French camp and siege area.
The northern approaches to Pavia.
Pavia itself along the southern portion of the battlefield.

Mirabello Park should not be interpreted as continuous woodland. It was a managed landscape containing open ground, woods, cultivated areas, orchards, gardens, roads, buildings and water features.

The existing Rev C battlefield geometry should be treated as authoritative for this scenario unless deliberately revised later. Exact historical locations of some gates, crossings and the Imperial breach remain reconstructed rather than certain.

metadata.title: Battle of Pavia
metadata.location: Mirabello Park, outside Pavia, Duchy of Milan

scenario.historicalSituation:
By February 1525, King Francis I of France had besieged the Imperial-held city of Pavia for several months. Antonio de Leyva's garrison continued to resist while an Imperial relief army under Charles de Lannoy, Fernando d'Avalos, Marquis of Pescara, and Georg von Frundsberg approached to break the siege.

Before dawn on 24 February, Imperial troops entered Mirabello Park through a breach in the park wall. The French army was dispersed around its siege positions and had to react to the unexpected Imperial advance.

The Imperial army entered the park with Spanish arquebusiers, German Landsknechts, cavalry and artillery. The French army included Francis I's gendarmes, a very large Swiss infantry body, the German Black Band, French infantry, artillery and additional mounted forces.

The scenario begins after the Imperial entry into Mirabello Park, before the historical outcome has been determined. The French player has the opportunity to organize a more effective response; the capture of Francis I and collapse of the French army are not scripted events.

The scenario represents the opening and main action as the Imperial relief force attempts to disrupt and defeat the French army inside Mirabello Park.

scenarioRules.title: Surprise
scenarioRules.text:
French formations that begin more than 18 inches from every Imperial unit begin Unalerted.

An Unalerted formation must pass a normal Battle Axe Command Test before it may activate.

Once a formation becomes Alerted, it remains Alerted for the rest of the game.

Historical basis: The Imperial army entered Mirabello Park before dawn and the dispersed French army had to respond to the unexpected attack.

Automation status recommendation: Review against current engine support. Do not mark automated until verified.
scenarioRules.evidence: Designer-created rule. No source evidence required.
scenarioRules.engineText: Scenario start: For each French command, if every unit in that command is more than 18" from every Imperial unit, set command state = Unalerted; otherwise set state = Alerted. When an Unalerted command attempts its first activation, make a normal Command Test. Pass: set Alerted permanently and allow normal activation. Fail: no units in that command may activate that turn; command remains Unalerted and may test again on a later turn.
